titulo: Review of the tenses: Future, conditional and hypotheses

aula.objetivo: Review and compare the B1 tenses: the past (present perfect, preterite, imperfect, pluperfect), the future, probability, the conditional, «si» hypotheses and the subjunctive, choosing each tense by the idea you want to express.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: the simple future (-é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án) is added to the infinitive: «hablaré», «comerás», «vivirá». Common irregulars: tendré, podré, haré, diré, pondré, saldré, vendré, querré, sabré, habré. STEP 2: the future also expresses probability in the present: «Ahora estará en casa» (He must be at home now / I suppose he's at home). And the future perfect expresses probability in the past: «Habrá salido ya» (He must have left already). STEP 3: the conditional (-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían) uses the same irregular stems: «tendría», «podría», «haría». It's used for politeness («¿Podría ayudarme?»), advice («Deberías descansar» — You should rest), the future seen from the past («Dijo que vendría» — He said he would come) and hypotheses. STEP 4: the conditional perfect (habría + past participle) expresses what would have happened: «Habría ido, pero estaba enfermo» (I would have gone, but I was ill). STEP 5: «si» hypotheses come in three types. If it's possible: «Si llueve, me quedo en casa» or «me quedaré» (si + present, no future after «si»). If it's unlikely or unreal in the present: «Si tuviera dinero, viajaría» (si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional). If it's unreal in the past: «Si hubiera sabido, habría venido» (si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect). STEP 6: never use the conditional or the future right after «si» in hypotheses. STEP 7: «quizá», «tal vez» and «posiblemente» take the subjunctive when there's doubt: «Quizá venga»; «a lo mejor» always takes the indicative: «A lo mejor viene».
blocos.comparacao: English "If I had money, I would travel" maps neatly onto «Si tuviera dinero, viajaría». The typical mistake comes from colloquial English "if I would have known": in Spanish the conditional never goes after «si» («si habría sabido» is wrong) — it's «si hubiera sabido, habría venido». And English "He must be at home" (a guess) is the future: «Estará en casa».

exemplos.pt: He must be at home now.
He said he would come on Monday.

exemplos.ru: Si llueve, me quedo en casa.
exemplos.pt: If it rains, I'll stay at home.
If I had money, I would travel.
If I had known, I would have come.

erros.motivo: After «si», the verb goes into the imperfect subjunctive, not the conditional.
In an unreal past hypothesis, use the pluperfect subjunctive after «si».

erros.errado: Si lloverá, me quedo en casa.
erros.certo: Si llueve, me quedo en casa.

erros.motivo: The imperfect subjunctive calls for the conditional in the other clause.

blocos.enunciado: Complete out loud with your own situation: «Si tuviera más tiempo, … Si hubiera nacido en otro país, … Si mañana hace buen tiempo, … Ahora mi mejor amigo estará …». Then say three polite sentences: «¿Podría…? Me gustaría… Habría preferido…».
Tell a short story in the past out loud with «mientras», «de repente» and «ya había».
